avatarPicker.dialog.description: How {name} appears in chats, Bots and desktops. An emoji and a colour make a team easy to tell apart at a glance.
avatarPicker.dialog.title: Avatar for {name}
botActivity.empty: This fills in as {name} works: each piece of work appears here when it starts, waits or finishes.
botActivity.feed.delegatorDecides: The delegator decides whether to continue
botActivity.feed.stopped: Work was stopped by its delegating Bot
botActivity.label: Activity
botActivity.schedule.body: Each entry wakes {name} at its time with the prompt as the task, in the background. Every start appears here as scheduled work.
botActivity.schedule.title: On a schedule
botApps.intro: Which of this workspace's connected apps {name} may use while it works. New apps are included when this is All.
botApps.none: No app is chosen: this Bot will not be offered any app.
botApps.roleNote: choose which apps a Bot may use
botApps.saved: Saved. The next run uses these apps.
botApps.soft: This limits what this Bot can do itself. A teammate that may use an app can still be asked to act, so keep an account that must stay separate in another workspace.
botApps.title: Apps this Bot may use
botDiary.confirmDelete: Delete this line from the diary?
botDiary.empty: No diary yet. The Bot writes one line here when each piece of work ends.
botDiary.intro: {name} writes one line here when each piece of work ends, and reads the last three days before starting new work. Delete a line that should not be remembered; nothing else can be changed here.
botDiary.label: Diary of {name}
botDiary.title: Diary
botIdentity.allowlistEmpty: No other bots in this workspace yet.
botIdentity.allowlistHelp: Teammates {name} may hand work to with message_bot. This routes messages; it is not access control.
botIdentity.connectorsHelp: Connector names, separated by commas. Each is offered to the Bot as a tool while it works.
botIdentity.intro: Who {name} is to the team. Changes reach the Bot when it starts its next work; work already in progress keeps its original settings.
botIdentity.name: @name
botIdentity.pauseIntro: Pausing stops {name} from being woken: schedules, other apps and chat messages are skipped. Work in progress finishes and waiting approvals stay as they are.
botIdentity.pausedNotice: Paused. Nothing new wakes the bot until it is resumed.
botIdentity.pausedSince: since {at}, by {by}. Schedules, other apps and chat messages are skipped; queued work waits.
botIdentity.reasoningHelp: Leave both on the default unless you are tuning how the AI thinks. Every piece of work records what it used.
botIdentity.renameHelp: Renaming moves the Bot home and working folder, renames its chat and updates teammates who may message it. It waits until {from} finishes its current work.
botIdentity.roleNote: change the Bot @name, job, teammates and thinking settings, or pause it
botIdentity.saved: Saved. The Bot uses this when it starts its next work.
botIdentity.title: Profile
botProfile.defaultTitle: People talk to this Bot first, and new chat channels connect to it
botProfile.experience.body: What {name} learned from past work, with links to its sources. Relevant entries help future runs; entries that need your confirmation are shown here. Your standing preferences and requirements are under Long-term instructions.
botProfile.experience.title: Experience
botProfile.glance.title: At a glance
botProfile.makeDefaultFailed: Could not make {name} the default Bot: {error}
botProfile.makeDefaultTitle: Make {name} the Bot people talk to first in this workspace
botProfile.pausedTitle: Schedules, other apps and chat messages do not wake this Bot until it is resumed.
botSchedules.empty: No schedules yet. Add one, for example weekdays at 09:00.
botSchedules.intro: Wake {name} at set times with a task, without anyone writing a message. Each occurrence is normal work and appears on the Activity tab. The repeat pattern uses minute, hour, day, month and weekday in {timeZone}; an occurrence is skipped if earlier work is still active.
botSchedules.nextUnavailable: Next occurrence unavailable for this draft.
botSchedules.paused: The Bot is paused; this schedule will not start until it is resumed.
botSchedules.runNowStarted: Schedule {number} started. Follow it in the bot's activity.
botSchedules.title: Schedules
contacts.botName.rule: Use letters A–Z, numbers, _ or -. This becomes the bot's @name.
contacts.dialog.description: A new teammate in {workspace}, on its shared computer. Give it an @name people will mention and a one-line job; you write its instructions on its profile afterwards.
contacts.dialog.draftRoleHelp: A model drafts its instructions for you to review. The bot starts after you apply or skip the draft.
contacts.dialog.draftRolePlaceholder: e.g. reviews pull requests and flags risky changes
contacts.dialog.rolePlaceholder: Reads dashboards and reports KPI changes
contacts.dialog.title: New Bot
contacts.heading: Bots
contacts.newContact.label: New Bot
contacts.next.createWorkspace.how: with New workspace in the workspace switcher
contacts.pick.body: Each bot is a teammate with a profile, an activity feed and a private chat.
contacts.pick.title: Pick a Bot
contacts.search.label: Search Bots
contacts.team.intro: Start a chat or catch up on your teammates’ work.
contacts.team.title: Your Bot team
management.model.cheapIntro: A second, cheaper AI model used for side work such as summaries and memory consolidation. It is not a router: the task itself always uses the AI model above, and nothing moves a request between models by price. Leave it on the server default unless you have a reason.
management.model.intro: Which AI model {name} thinks with. The server default moves every Bot that did not pick its own when it changes.
management.model.label: Model
management.model.title: Model
management.rules.byHandIntro: A rule matches a tool, and optionally the site, a text the arguments must contain, or a file path. Only the tool is required; the fewer fields, the wider the rule.
management.rules.empty: No rules yet: every outside action still asks.
management.rules.intro: When {name} is about to do something with an outside effect, such as clicking Export, submitting a form or sending a message, it stops and asks in the chat. A rule answers in advance so the same action does not ask again. The easiest way to make one is the Always button on a request; here you can read, remove, or write one by hand.
management.rules.roleNote: write or remove an approval rule
management.rules.title: Approval rules
management.soul.changed: SOUL.md changed since it was loaded. Your draft is preserved.
management.soul.intro: Who {name} is and how it works, in plain Markdown (its SOUL.md). Add responsibilities, working preferences and what a good result looks like. Saving takes effect on its next work.
management.soul.keepDraft: Keep draft and use latest as base
management.soul.saved: SOUL.md saved. The next work starts a fresh session with this version.
management.soul.savedNextRun: SOUL.md saved. The Bot is busy now; its next work starts a fresh session with this version.
management.soul.title: Instructions
management.soulDraft.applied: Applied. The next work starts a fresh session with these instructions.
management.soulDraft.failed: No draft: {error}. The saved instructions are unchanged.
management.soulDraft.instructionPlacehol: e.g. also review release notes, be more concise
management.soulDraft.intro: Describe the change in one sentence or a few keywords. A model drafts it; nothing is saved until you apply it.
management.soulDraft.noPermissions: Instructions describe behaviour only. They never grant tools, approvals, network access or authority.
management.soulDraft.pending: Drafting… This is recorded AI work and is billed to this workspace.
management.soulDraft.previewIntro: Proposed change against the loaded version. Lines marked + are added and - removed; everything else stays as it is.
management.soulDraft.saveFirst: Save or discard your own edits first.
management.soulDraft.stale: The instructions changed since this draft was made. Discard it and draft again against the current version.
management.soulDraft.title: Draft with AI
management.tryIt.intro: Opens a private chat named “Test {name}”. It is normal work with the same limits, record and costs.
management.tryIt.title: Try it
management.vision.label: Image input on {model}:
management.vision.reason.blocked: no Bot in this workspace can start the test
management.vision.reason.explicit_refusa: the model said it cannot see images
management.vision.reason.no_transport_ev: no image was seen on the way to the model
management.vision.reason.not_probed: not tested for this configuration yet
management.vision.reason.wrong_answer: the test answer was wrong, so the model may describe images it cannot see
management.vision.withheld: This AI model is not shown images: pictures and screenshots reach it as a short text notice instead.
ruleVersions.confirmRestore: Save version {version} again as the newest version?
ruleVersions.intro: Every save of {file} is kept. Compare any two, or restore one: a restore saves it again as the newest version and {name} uses it for its next work.
ruleVersions.restoredNextRun: Version {from} restored as version {to}. The Bot is busy now; it uses this for its next work.
